why: Commit messages reach agents through git log and PR tooling, and rebar-check trims them (a trailing U+FEFF was measured gone), so this rule reads history raw. The fail side has one commit whose message carries U+200B inside a word, committed verbatim from bytes. The pass side has the same tree and two honest messages that carry invisibles by accident: one opens with the UTF-8 byte-order mark Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes and `git commit -F` keeps, which is consumed like a file's BOM; the other is a Dependabot body where GitHub put U+200B between '@' and a login so nobody gets pinged. Stop reading commits, or read them through a trimming helper, and the fail side goes green; drop either exemption and the pass side goes red.
